elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained opener of the capping sentence reads "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT ... EXCEED"; the redline does not disturb the bilateral "either party" formulation.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered cap is "THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION" — no USD 1,000,000 alternative floor, "actually paid" rather than "paid or payable", and the anchor is the filing of the cause of action rather than the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Second sentence retained: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS ... OR FOR ANY INDIRECT, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Inserted into the cap exception opener: "EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 ..., A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS, ...".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The exception list covers only Section 8, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears in the rendered text.

Pre-existing carve-out retained: "EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT", which the finding identifies as the indemnification section; the cross-reference is unchanged and remains operative.
Inserted: "OR A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" within the cap exception opener.
Same inserted phrase: "A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT".
No fraud carve-out appears anywhere in the rendered Section 9 exception list.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The only IP-adjacent exception is the Section 8 cross-reference (an indemnity), which is not an express carve-out for a party's own infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the rendered language states that Corio's obligation to pay fees is not "damages" for cap purposes; the cap as drafted could be read to limit recovery of unpaid fees.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ... EXCEED" — bilateral cap retained unchanged; no unlimited-Customer-liability language remains (deterministic check confirmed).

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Deletion of "FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO" leaves "THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION" — a full 12-months-of-fees basis; "paid" vs "paid or payable" is a preferred-only refinement.
Existing "EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT" carve-out preserved in both the cap sentence and the consequential-damages sentence.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Added "A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" to the cap exception, mutual in direction ("a party's").
Added "A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE" to the cap exception.
Added "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" in the same mutual exception phrase.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: mutuality and the Section 8 indemnity carve-out survive untouched, the per-transaction narrowing is deleted so the cap now runs to all fees paid in the 12 months, and confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct are added to the existing exception opener.

Preferred level fails on six elements: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, "actually paid" rather than "paid or payable", anchor tied to filing of the cause of action rather than the event giving rise to the claim, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud, or infringement of the other party's IP; the Customer payment-obligation exclusion is also absent.

Minimality holds: only two surgical changes were made (strike "FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO"; insert three carve-outs into the existing exception opener). The mutual consequential-damages waiver, the Section 8 references and the reasonable-allocation-of-risk sentence are all retained, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, additional damages categories) were added.

Intent preserved: the amendment leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined term, keeps the bilateral structure and the existing risk-allocation acknowledgement, and creates no contradiction with the retained second sentence.

Residual point for the drafter (not a defect at fallback): the element "Indemnification obligations are uncapped" rests entirely on the retained "Section 8" cross-reference — confirm Section 8 is in fact the indemnification section, since if it is a warranty section the fallback carve-out would fail.

To reach the preferred position, the drafter would need to add the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, change "ACTUALLY PAID" to "paid or payable", re-anchor to "the event giving rise to the claim", and extend the exception list to data protection and security obligations, fraud, and infringement of the other party's intellectual property, plus a sentence that Corio's payment obligations are not subject to the cap.
